question: Another two new Guardia Civil officers have died on duty while pursuing a drug trafficking speedboat in Huelva, at a time of a concerning increase in criminal networks in the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. In recent years, the Guardia Civil and the National Police have warned of the material disadvantage their agents face in combating drug trafficking.

Parliament’s PETI Committee adopted a report in November 2025 calling on the Spanish Government to protect agents fighting drug trafficking by providing more resources, legal protection and tougher penalties for criminal organisations.

In view of the above: Has the Spanish Government informed the Commission of any progress in strengthening operational capacities, resources at sea or legal protection for law enforcement agencies tackling drug trafficking since Parliament’s report was adopted?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.7.2026) The fight against drug trafficking is a priority of the Commission1. The Commission is working with Member States to effectively implement the EU Drugs Strategy2 and the EU Action Plan to fight drug trafficking in line with the European Council conclusions of 16 June 20263.

The EU Action Plan to fight drug trafficking aims to address the misuse of high-speed vessels and foster innovative technologies to detect drugs trafficking in high-risk areas and transport hubs. Maintaining law and order and safeguarding internal security are the responsibility of Member States, in line with Article 72 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

Under EMPACT 2026–20294, drug trafficking remains a core EU priority. Spain leads the operational action plan on cannabis, cocaine and heroin trafficking and is a Member of the Maritime Analysis and Operations Centre – Narcotics5 funded by the Internal Security Fund.

This framework supports coordination, maritime intelligence, port cooperation and action against criminal networks using Atlantic and Mediterranean routes, including the threat of gofast vessels and infiltration of organised crime in ports.
1 COM(2025)744 final. 2 COM(2025)743 final. 3 EUCO 8/26. 4 The new European Multidisciplinary Platform Against Criminal Threats Council Conclusions 9397/25. 5 https://maoc.eu/.
